title: How the band got the name Original Tuxedo from Sim Black
summary: Ridgley tells how Sim Black, master of Boy Scout troop 13, suggested the name and tuxedo outfits, and about playing for the Scouts at Kentwood. Allen suggests tracking Black down.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: For a club, one of the clubs that had you in the city of New Orleans, which is a colored club, and we wanted quadrillo. And we played for them. But I never didn't know much about playing a quadrillo. That wasn't in my time of playing music, you see. But I have seen them dance quadrillo before that, you see. I've seen them dance quadrillo. Now our tuxedo band, you see, many people want to know how the band got to be named the original tuxedo orchestra. See, we used to call it tuxedo band, well of course there wasn't a problem. We called it tuxedo jazz band. And I had a band headquarters on Howard Avenue between Drive and Barone. We had a pressing shop there. And we used to do a lot of work for the Boy Scouts for everybody in them days, you see. Now the man that made a suggestion for us to call our band the original tuxedo, his name was Mr. Sim Black. He was a master of Boy Scout troop 13, and he thought a whole lot of our band. So he came to a pressing shop one morning. He said, Ridley, I come down and have a little talk with you. He says, I believe that I have something that will do the band good. And he said, I was thinking that you all, I said, now the debutante season is about to open. You see, it falls in the air. And I would suggest that you all get black tuxedo suits, derby hats, you see, white tie, you know, black shoes coming in. He says, and call the band the original tuxedo band. And Mr. Sim Black, master of Boy Scout troop 13, give us the, I made a suggestion for us to name the band, the original tuxedo band. I've heard so many stories about it, and none of them didn't know who named the band. But Mr. Sim Black, master of Boy Scout troop 13. So we used to play for them, them boys, all the time. We even went to Kentwood with them when they was on the vacation in the summertime. They was in Kentwood out in the swamp. And we had an occasion to go to Kentwood to play. And so we notified them that we was coming to Kentwood. And they made it possible to meet us at the train, the morning train, took us out in the swamp. And we spent all day with troop site team out in the swamp. And they treated us well. They fed us and everything. And when time was to come and play our job up in the town, they brought us back up in town. And when we, and they came home from that vacation trip, but we almost played a dance at each one of those boys' houses. They just thought so much of the band and the toilet pops and everything about it. And they just wanted to do a dance at each other. They wanted the band and just wanted to give a dance. And so that helped us a whole lot. Mr. Sim Black, he was a very nice man. He took great, he entered his own band. He got many a jobs. I don't know whether he was living there or whether he was there or not. So there was a great man that had lives and young men and things in this town. All the men there now that was on that trip.
Is Sim Black about your age?
He was about my age, yeah. He could be living, Mr. Black. He could be living.
Well, we might try to find him. He might be alive.
He might be alive. He can't tell him. I said his name is Sim Black. Well we can look him up in the city directory, you know they've got everybody's names.
Yeah, and then you know how to find him too.
So that helped us a whole lot from that. We played all those fraternity dances.
